title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover during load spikes
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: During a customer incident on 2026-02-18 we observed the SLO enforcer enter a pathological backoff cycle combined with aggressive load-shedding which prevented regional failover from triggering cleanly. This caused increased 5xx rates for synthetic traffic and degraded tail latency for some tenants. Motivation: stabilize SLO enforcer state transitions, ensure backoff hysteresis prevents rapid thrashing, and make regional failover path tolerant to transient shed events. Changes: 1) tighten and document hysteresis in the backoff state machine (increase min-backoff window and add admission-count decay), 2) decouple load-shedding decision from immediate failover trigger (introduce a failover-eligibility window to avoid flapping), 3) fix a race in the quorum check that could mark a region as unhealthy when KV heartbeat lagged, 4) add additional observability (metrics + labels) around per-tenant shed decisions and failover triggers. Checklist: - [x] reproduce locally with perf-canary harness - [x] e2e test added in perf-canary and smoke tests - [x] staged rollout to dedicated Canary pool - [x] added metrics and dashboard panels for correlation - [x] rollback path validated (feature flag + manual rollback) Testing: local unit tests for state transitions, perf-canary simulation showing no thrash under synthetic spike, manual chaos runs to validate failover eligibility window. Rollout: gated by feature flag `slo_enforcer_stable_backoff_v2` and a gradual 10/30/60/100% rollout to production. If we see regressions, feature-flag off will revert behavior immediately. Related: ENG-5423 investigated incident; SUP-1892 is the customer support ticket tied to the outage. Merge method: squash merge to release/v1.12.0. Notes: this is a targeted hotfix focused on operational stability; no model-serving API changes.
